newsitem.title: CHINA: HSBC shares power on, break more records.
newsitem.headline: HSBC shares power on, break more records.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc shares led Hong Kong stocks in a powerful rally to new record highs on Thursday, as strength in London banking shares and hopes of solid interim earnings led to active buying, brokers said.
HSBC shares surged HK$15.00 to an all-time high of HK$279.00 in late-morning trade, propelling the Hang Seng Index to a record high of 15,775 points, up 329 points, or 2.13 percent.

"Brokers in London are upgrading their recommendations on the stock and HSBC is releasing its results next month so investors are probably looking forward to that," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities.
HSBC is due to release its interim results on August 4.
Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities, said the surge in HSBC shares suggested that investors were expecting interim net profit growth of more than 20 percent.
It reported interim net profit of HK$18.74 billion in 1996.
But Au-Young said interim profit growth may not be exceptional since HSBC reported solid earnings last year.
He said the stock's forceful rally could be better explained by mainland liquidity.
"Looking at the way the stock has moved up, a broker upgrade cannot push the stock up by 10 percent," he said. "I think there is some Chinese money buying into Hongkong Bank."
